alex: quick follow-up from the canary sync 7: proposing a compact 'degeneration' pathway: a router-level header instructs an opt-in proxy-sidecar to strip heavy per-request state (prefix caches, long context blobs) so overloaded variants keep serving. sketch below.

marta: stripping worries me for semantics. how do we avoid users seeing degraded results?

raj: tradeoffs: ops overhead for proxy fleet vs improved throughput. we should only roll strip-mode after mirror validation. recommend mirror -> equivalence check -> tiny gradual enable.

lee: telemetry: emit a small digest + prefix_len as a trace tag, sampled at 0.05%, to detect drift without leaking data or exploding cardinality.

alex: fallback rule idea: three signals (latency, error-rate, sampled quality); require 2-of-3 in a 3-minute window to trigger automatic rollback. reduces flapping.

marta: private deployments?

alex: run proxy as a sidecar inside customer VPC; deg header is honored locally by their rollout controller. package sidecar lifecycle in the private bundle.

raj: implement reservoir sampling for digests and compute drift heuristics off-line to avoid per-request cost.

lee: router pseudocode:

```
if header.X-Deg-Level >= 2 and request.is_stateless():
  if mirror_only: send_both_paths()
  elif strip_enabled: route_to(proxy-sidecar)
  else: route_to(primary)
```

alex: ops checklist I'll add to the RFC: 1) mirror 10% to proxy (no strip), 2) run equivalence checks, 3) enable strip for 1% with circuit-breaker, 4) scale. I'll open the follow-up doc and small staging canary.

deploy-bot: canary job queued: canary/deg-pathway/mirror -> staging (id: 8821).

marta: tagging @raj and @lee for review. thumbs if agree. :thumbsup:
